'''Zoran Planinić''' (born September 12, 1982) is a Croatian former professional [[basketball]] player.

==Early years==
Planinić was born in [[Mostar]], [[Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina|Bosnia and Herzegovina]], in the [[Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia|former Yugoslavia]]. He started his basketball career at [[HKK Brotnjo|HKK Brotnjo Čitluk]] from [[Čitluk, Bosnia and Herzegovina|Čitluk]], Bosnia and Herzegovina and was noticed by [[KK Cibona]] where he continued his junior career.<ref name="hrsport">{{cite web | url = http://www.hrsport.net/vijesti/402557 | language = hr | title = Njegov doprinos vrlo važan | publisher = hrsport.net | date = 2010-08-25 | access-date = 2011-08-11}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Zoran Planinić|url=http://www.brotnjo-sport.info/index.php/sportske-vedete-brotnja/zoran-planinic|website=Brotnjo Sport|publisher=brotnjo-sport.info|access-date=1 December 2015}}</ref>

==Professional career==
In the 1999–2000 season, Planinić started his professional career on loan to [[KK Dubrava|Benston Zagreb]].<ref name="hrsport"/>

He returned to [[KK Cibona|Cibona Zagreb]] in 2000 and he was named the [[HT Premijer liga|Croatian League]] [[Most valuable player|MVP]] in 2001. He stayed with Cibona until 2003.

In the [[2003 NBA draft]], the {{convert|6|ft|7|in|cm|-tall|adj=mid}} (in shoes),<ref>[http://www.nba.com/playerfile/zoran_planinic/ NBA.com Official Player Profile.]</ref> {{convert|210|lb|adj=on}} [[point guard]]/[[shooting guard]] was drafted 22nd overall by the [[Brooklyn Nets#New Jersey Nets|New Jersey Nets]]. In three NBA seasons he averaged 4 points, 1.4 rebounds and 1.1 assists per game. Planinić's three NBA seasons were not notable, with his only distinguishing moment coming in the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]], when he hit a spectacular full-court, 77-foot, 3rd-quarter-ending buzzer beater at a home win, on 9 November 2005, against the [[2005–06 Utah Jazz season|Utah Jazz]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20190101002911/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=251109017 Carter scores 21 as Nets cruise past Jazz.]</ref>

Planinić's final NBA game was Game 2 of the 2006 Eastern Conference Semi-finals on 10 May 2006 against the [[2005–06 Miami Heat season|Miami Heat]]. New Jersey lost the game 89 - 111, with Planinić recording one assist and one steal.

[[File:ZoranPlaninic01.jpg|thumb|upright|right|Zoran Planinić warming up in the second game of the 2008 [[Liga ACB|Spanish ACB League]] Finals]]
In the summer of 2006, Planinić and the [[Brooklyn Nets#New Jersey Nets|Nets]] agreed to a buyout, in which he was sent back to Europe to spend the season with [[Saski Baskonia|TAU Cerámica]] of the [[Liga ACB|Spanish ACB League]], a team that also featured talented [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] prospect [[Tiago Splitter]]. With TAU Cerámica, Planinić won the [[Supercopa de España de Baloncesto|Spanish Supercup]] championship in both 2006 and 2007, and the Spanish League championship in 2008.

On 25 June 2008 Planinić signed a two-year contract with the [[Russian Basketball Super League 1|Russian Superleague A]] club [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]].<ref>[http://www.cskabasket.com/news/?a=news&id=5471&lang=en CSKA Moscow signs Planinic to 2 year deal.]</ref> On 17 June 2010, he signed a 2+1 year contract with the [[Russian Professional Basketball League|Russian PBL]] club [[BC Khimki]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cskabasket.com/news/?a=news&id=8304&lang=en |title=Zoran Planinic will continue his career in Khimki |access-date=2010-07-13 |archive-date=2012-03-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120306075725/http://www.cskabasket.com/news/?a=news&id=8304&lang=en |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 27 July 2013 he signed a two-year contract with [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/turkey/60326/anadolu-efes-officially-sign-zoran-planinic.html Anadolu Efes officially sign Zoran Planinic]</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=ANADOLU EFES plans future with Planinic|url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2013-14-signings/i/115085/8177|work=Euroleague.net|access-date=27 July 2013}}</ref> In January 2014, he hit a long-range [[buzzer beater]] in the last second of the game to defeat [[Pallacanestro Olimpia Milano|Olimpia Milano]] by a score of 61–60.<ref>{{cite news|title=Zoran Planinic scores the most incredible game winning buzzer beater you'll ever see|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/euroleague/110783/zoran-planinic-scores-the-most-incredible-game-winning-buzzer-beater-you-ll-ever-see.html|access-date=14 October 2014|work=sportando.com}}</ref> In his first season with the team, he averaged 8.4 points and 3.7 assists, over 23 [[2013–14 Euroleague|EuroLeague]] games. In the summer of 2014, [[Dušan Ivković]] was appointed as Efes' head coach, and Planinić lost his place in the team. Despite that, he was still under contract for the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=OTAC DARIJA ŠARIĆ U ŠOKU 'Ivkovićevi potezi su suludi, možda ćemo tražiti raskid!'|url=http://www.jutarnji.hr/saric-senior-u-soku--ivkovicevi-potezi-su-suludi--mozda-cemo-traziti-raskid--/1227678/|access-date=14 October 2014|work=jutarnji.hr|language=hr}}</ref>

==Croatian national team==
Planinić was part of the Croatian junior national teams that won the bronze medal at the 1999 [[FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|FIBA Under-19 World Cup]] and the silver medal at the 2001 [[FIBA Under-21 World Championship|FIBA Under-21 World Cup]].

Planinić was also a part of the senior men's [[Croatia men's national basketball team|Croatian national basketball teams]] at [[EuroBasket]]s [[EuroBasket 2003|2003]], [[EuroBasket 2005|2005]], [[EuroBasket 2007|2007]] and [[EuroBasket 2009|2009]].

==Personal life==
[[Ivica Zubac]], who plays for the [[Indiana Pacers]] as of 2026, is Planinić's cousin.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/1058267/ivica-zubac-credits-cousin-zoran-planinic-for-his-motivation/ | title=Ivica Zubac credits cousin Zoran Planinic for his motivation | date=11 May 2020 }}</ref>
